findings.observation: All 63 opaque compute contracts have one root selector and no output_parts. ir_021 builds six independently sourced settings fields but its whole-output rule consumes all five environment bindings plus cwd. ir_319 maps independent inspection fields under a single whole-output rule.
findings.meaning: There is no output-specific rule separating a demand for propertyId from clientEmail/resultsDir, or verdict from other inspection fields. Whole-output rules must not serve as precise rules for arbitrary child output fields.
findings.review_needed: Use source-supported field selectors/decomposition or deterministic structure for these explicit composite results. This audit does not execute the demand engine or claim its resulting status.

findings.observation: The report input contracts require entire dateRanges/dimensions/metrics values. Their cited evidence is the current request construction; ir_119 says the actual request has these fields. DateRange declares startDate/endDate and object ranges pass through unchanged.
findings.meaning: The current argument shape alone does not prove every nested field is necessary or that the interface requires the whole nested value. Passed-through date objects make this relevant to extra-field detection.
findings.review_needed: Independently justify necessary nested selectors and collection structure from interface/source semantics. Retain whole values only where actually required. No concrete secret field or deletion result is asserted.

findings.observation: The original CFG retains client handle and request as separate inputs. The selected remote call references only request input 1. The ir_119 processing gap explicitly records that the flat format lacks a separate dynamic receiver reference.
findings.meaning: Complete contract row indexing relative to the call operation is not complete receiver/credential dependency coverage of the source invocation.
findings.review_needed: Retain the receiver occurrence and scoped gap; never infer nonnecessity merely from the missing operation operand. No propagation outcome is claimed.

findings.observation: Source destructures filters/orderBy. The CFG preserves them in unused metadata and source text, while output bindings and processing select_part operations cover only dimensions/metrics/dateRange/limit/save.
findings.meaning: The original source occurrence remains recorded, but this snapshot does not establish a distinct forward field-read/observation for the unused fields.
findings.review_needed: Keep actual reads distinct from absence in the remote request; do not report these fields as never read or already proven deletable.

positive_samples.observation: Scalar property-name formatting requires only settings.propertyId and excludes the remaining fields while retaining the actual settings input.
Validation distinguishes truth of propertyId/clientEmail/privateKey from their full values; its composite output still lacks separate selectors.
Count messages require dimensions/metrics cardinality when present, excluding member contents while retaining the actual metadata input.
Whole-wrapper value is justified by complete JSON.stringify serialization. It does not by itself make the save action task-required.
The deterministic build retains individual request-field inputs instead of overriding structure with a semantic contract.

processing_gaps.reason: The zero-argument library boundary and distinct environment post-state are supported. Exact bindings populated from a given .env, precedence against preexisting values and initializer error handling inside the dependency require its implementation or an applicable interface contract.

The setup command and its status are modeled. The lockfile provides distribution URLs, while this command alone leaves the actual registry or cache acquisitions, lifecycle behavior and installed file set unresolved.

The supplied call supplies its concrete SDK receiver as well as the request. The flat call format has a fixed location and ordered request arguments and has no separate dynamic receiver reference. The request pairing is retained at this coordinate. Exact underlying transport, authentication exchanges and wire fields remain inside the SDK.

This acquisition needs the freshly selected property name, the particular client handle and the first SDK tuple member. The grouped CFG operands identify the getters as resources. The distinct receiver and property values are missing from the call operands.

The source sends the current prefixed property plus /metadata through the acquired client and receives the first full SDK result before dimension projection. The grouped operands lack the actual receiver and formatted request name bindings.

The source sends the current prefixed property plus /metadata through the acquired client and receives the first full SDK result before metric projection. The grouped operands lack the actual receiver and formatted request name bindings.

The source sends the current prefixed property plus /metadata through the acquired client and returns the first SDK result in full. The grouped operands lack the actual receiver and formatted request name bindings.

The reference says impressions and the Skill and direct help say clicks. The actual page query supplies the page dimension and a row limit of 100, with no ranking criterion or local sort. The supplied evidence leaves the relationship between these ranking descriptions and the returned order unresolved.

The Skill lists flexible ranges broadly. Search Console documents calendar dates and forwards object endpoints unchanged. Runtime acceptance of a GA4-relative object by the Search Console recipient remains unresolved.
The reference describes an array payload and the implementation saves and returns an object containing the dimensions array. The array description does not establish another projection boundary.
The reference describes an array payload and the implementation saves and returns an object containing the metrics array. The array description does not establish another projection boundary.

The log receives a message containing the current URL before SDK entry and can itself throw. The compact protected-call result represents the normal append and the caught value. Its post-entry error case does not distinguish SDK rejection from a normal response followed by mapping or append failure. The exception is scoped to this occurrence in both cases.

Its post-entry error case does not distinguish SDK rejection from a normal response followed by mapping or append failure. The exception is scoped to this occurrence in both cases.

The write uses replace at the selected runtime path. Its second-resolution local timestamp, sanitized name and optional suffix can collide with another invocation. These operands establish the path for this write and leave ownership of a later read unresolved.

The path is linked to the file access, but the format has no separate read selector for an existence result versus UTF-8 content at the same storage location. Normal read content and the caught read failure remain distinct.

The Skill requires analysis, timestamped JSON saving, reading the saved JSON, and a Markdown summary in results/summaries/ with tables, trends and recommendations. The analysis entry points discard their save paths. Listing and substring matching establish candidate paths and load reads independently. The supplied implementation lacks a binding from a particular analysis invocation to selected file content and lacks a summary writer or user delivery. A model processing the returned JSON may observe the whole parsed version under EM02 and EM03. That possibility does not establish field-level necessity, a raw UTF-8 model observation, a particular number of model stages, or which fields a Markdown writer consumes.

actual_inputs.value:
GA4 Analytics Toolkit
=====================

GA4 High-level functions:
  - siteOverview(dateRange?)        Comprehensive site snapshot
  - trafficAnalysis(dateRange?)     Deep dive on sources
  - contentPerformance(dateRange?)  Top pages analysis
  - userBehavior(dateRange?)        Engagement patterns
  - compareDateRanges(range1, range2) Compare two date ranges
  - liveSnapshot()                  Real-time data

Search Console functions:
  - searchConsoleOverview(dateRange?)  Combined SEO snapshot
  - keywordAnalysis(dateRange?)        Query/keyword analysis
  - seoPagePerformance(dateRange?)     Page-level SEO metrics
  - getTopQueries(dateRange?)          Top search queries
  - getTopPages(dateRange?)            Top pages by clicks
  - getDevicePerformance(dateRange?)   Mobile vs desktop
  - getCountryPerformance(dateRange?)  Traffic by country

Indexing functions:
  - reindexUrls(urls)                  Request re-indexing for URLs
  - checkIndexStatus(urls)             Check if URLs are indexed
  - requestIndexing(url)               Request single URL re-crawl
  - inspectUrl(url)                    Inspect URL index status

Low-level GA4 functions:
  - runReport({ dimensions, metrics, dateRange })
  - getPageViews(dateRange?)
  - getTrafficSources(dateRange?)
  - getUserDemographics(dateRange?)
  - getEventCounts(dateRange?)
  - getActiveUsers()
  - getRealtimeEvents()
  - getPropertyMetadata()

All results are automatically saved to /results directory.
